spec_match.rationale: Shows the practical payoff the CSSWG resolution was aimed at — a token sheet where only deliberate departures remain — and backs the equivalence claim with real registrations and computed-style comparison rather than assertion.

interactive.rationale: The token-count slider regenerates both sheets and the savings stats live (verified at load via the auto-run render), and Apply performs sixteen real CSS.registerProperty calls then compares the two cards' computed padding, radius and colour.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises a realistic token stylesheet both ways, applied live to the same component, with boilerplate counted and rendering confirmed identical — all present.

edge_cases.rationale: The pre-156 rejection path is handled with honest copy and per-run name prefixes avoid the register-once trap, but the 'identical rendering' check sets every value directly on the card, so the one real behavioural divergence between the sheets — omitted inherits making tokens inherit — can never show up in the comparison.

references.rationale: See-also links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5168674259468288 and the @property spec section.

conformance.rationale: The feature-level suite covers the omission contracts this page relies on plus unchanged negatives; on Chromium 141 the /conformance/ route executed 4 pass / 4 fail, the expected split for a pre-156 browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): load-time render verified via console ('24 tokens: 120 lines -> 72 lines') and both screenshots showing the two sheets, counts and stats populated; the slider and the Apply comparison are input-driven and could not be exercised headlessly, so their behaviour is judged from the source wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert reports 'token-sheets-applied' with before/after acceptance counts and the identical verdict, and the console carries only the page's own labelled logs.

design_system.rationale: Everything is built from design-system variables, the Apply button overrides background and color together, stats and sheets sit on approved backgrounds, and no static-card pattern appears.

accessibility.rationale: The slider is a native range input inside a labelled control with a live count, sheet pre blocks are keyboard-reachable via tabindex, outcome copy lands in an aria-live=polite output, and stats use a definition list.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At true 360px the sheets and stats stack to one column with internal pre scrolling and no page-level horizontal overflow; at 1280px they sit side by side; slider and button meet 44px targets on both.

openQuestions.title: Equivalence check cannot detect the inherits divergence
openQuestions.detail: Apply sets each token's value directly on the card element, then compares computed styles. Because values are set on the element itself, inheritance never comes into play, so the comparison would report 'identical' even though the after-sheet tokens (no inherits descriptor) inherit and the before-sheet tokens do not. A nested child element reading the tokens without local values would expose the one genuine behavioural difference between the two sheets — worth adding so 'the same result' is demonstrated honestly rather than by construction.

openQuestions.title: Lede claims 'a third shorter' while the live stat says 48%
openQuestions.detail: The intro copy says the sheet 'gets a third shorter' but the measured reduction at the default 24 tokens is 48%, and the stat panel says so. Either soften the lede ('roughly half') or make it defer to the live number.

openQuestions.title: Displayed @property sheets are not what gets registered
openQuestions.detail: The two pre blocks render @property rule text while Apply registers via CSS.registerProperty under per-run suffixed names. The equivalence is real but the mechanism differs from what is shown; a sentence noting that the registrations run through the CSSOM API (or an actual injected stylesheet, see the at-property-parse-probe question on descriptor-lab) would close the gap between the code shown and the code run.

summary: A convincing practical-use-case page: the slider genuinely regenerates both token sheets with live line/character savings (auto-run verified: console logged '24 tokens: 120 lines -> 72 lines'), and Apply registers both variants for real before comparing computed styles, with an honest pre-156 rejection branch. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v156/optional-descriptors-for-registered-custom-properties/token-sheet-diff/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump, clean console, feature /conformance/ route 4 pass / 4 fail as expected pre-156). The substantive gap is that the identical-rendering comparison sets values on the compared element directly, so it can never surface the inheritance difference that omitting inherits actually introduces — the demo proves equivalence for the case it constructs rather than the general one.
